segmentation.text: the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
who intends to exit a roundabout
Shall use the left lane to turn left or complete a U-turn

elements.justification: "vehicles" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed as one atom, never expanded; its exclusions are the reading's classification. "within a roundabout": st.roundabout "a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches" carries DEF-LVMC-11-02-130 ("an intersection characterized by a circulatory roadway", including the crosswalks on the entering and exiting roadways) at its whole extent; rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region" anchors the subject to that roundabout, so no other roundabout of the scene is read. Same mapping as the index for "the operation of vehicles" and "within a roundabout".

"a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "The operator" names who controls it, a relational role and no aggregate, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). Same mapping as the index entry "The operator of a vehicle".

The intention to exit is not observable; it is read through the exit it leads to (observable_reading intention): the observation at which the subject's footprint (rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region") ceases to overlap the roundabout r (st.roundabout) it occupied, which is the recognition of the turn concepts ("The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r"). No declared intention: the words state an intention to exit, which is read by the exit made, and the turn they name is read by the heading change the concepts measure.

"to turn left or complete a U-turn": drv.motion.left_turn_through_region ("a turn to the left through region r ... heading change ... from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive") and drv.motion.u_turn_through_region ("so as to proceed in the opposite direction" through r), taking r = the roundabout the subject exits; a heading change measured from the entry into the roundabout to the exit is the turn the vehicle makes by the roundabout, whatever the circulation in between. "use the left lane": st.lane "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles" with st.lane_adjacency "lane ordinal within the carriageway ... ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction": "the left lane" is the lane of ordinal 1, the count literal 1 declared on this span (literals), whose value is fixed by the atom's contract, not a reading parameter; rel.occupies anchors the lanes the subject's footprint overlaps. Not a stand-in exclusions: lane membership is read by footprint overlap and ordinal, never by a lateral offset from the edge, and the ordinal is not the marking between lanes.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). Bind a region r of kind st.roundabout. At the judged observation the subject exits r having turned left or completed a U-turn through it: drv_motion_left_turn_through_region(subject, r) or drv_motion_u_turn_through_region(subject, r) rises, each with step .param p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph and turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min (the U-turn concept takes step and u_turn_min only). The intention to exit is read through this exit.
obligation: Re-bind the same roundabout: a region r of kind st.roundabout for which the same concept rises for the subject at the judged observation. The subject used the left lane within r: at every observation from its entry into r (the latest observation at which rel.occupies(subject, r) rose) up to the judged observation, wherever rel.occupies(subject, r) holds, every region l of kind st.lane with rel.occupies(subject, l) has st_lane_adjacency_ordinal(l) equal to the declared count literal 1 of s5 ("the left lane", the leftmost lane by st.lane_adjacency's contract). Written with since: since(phi, rises(occupies(subject, r)) and phi), phi = occupies(subject, r) implies forall lane l (occupies(subject, l) implies ordinal(l) = 1). Unknown where the entry lies before the recording or an ordinal of an occupied lane is unobserved.

narrowings.why: "The operator" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle whoever or whatever controls it.

"who intends to exit a roundabout" is read through the exit itself: the duty is judged at the observation at which the vehicle leaves the roundabout, the recognition of the turn; a vehicle that intends to exit but has not yet left is judged when it leaves.

"use the left lane" is read as occupying, within the roundabout, no lane other than the lane of ordinal 1 of its carriageway from the entry to the exit; a footprint straddling the left lane and another lane is not use of the left lane alone. A single-lane roundabout's only lane is ordinal 1.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A two-lane roundabout r (st.roundabout) whose circulatory and approach lanes carry st.lane_adjacency ordinals 1 (inner, leftmost) and 2 (outer). The subject, a passenger car (ru.motor_vehicle), enters r heading east in the lane of ordinal 2, circulates counter-clockwise in the outer lane and leaves r heading north: its yaw rate, observed at every scene at the sampling standard, integrates to a quarter turn to the left since the entry. At the exit the left turn through r is recognized; the subject occupied a lane of ordinal 2 within r.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout and the same left turn, but the subject enters and circulates in the lane of ordinal 1 only and leaves r heading north.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject enters heading east in the lane of ordinal 2 and leaves at the first exit heading south, a quarter turn to the right since the entry: no left turn or U-turn is recognized.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not supply lane ordinals (st.lane_adjacency absent): which lane the subject used is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject enters heading east in the lane of ordinal 2, circulates and leaves heading west, a half turn to the left since the entry: a U-turn through r made from the outer lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject makes the U-turn of branch_1 in the lane of ordinal 1 throughout.

onset.words: the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
onset.justification: The act begins at the subject's entry into the roundabout: the observation at which rel.occupies(subject, r) rose, the onset the concepts declare ("its entry into r").

occasion.recognition: who intends to exit a roundabout

under_way.words: to turn left or complete a U-turn
under_way.justification: Inside the act the subject's heading change since its entry into r (headingSince, integrated from kin.yaw_rate "rate of change of heading") is defined and the subject's footprint overlaps r; before the entry it is not. The heading's integration reads the subject's motion, not the place alone.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: turning-movement classification in intersection geometric design practice (AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets)

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: turning-movement classification in intersection geometric design practice (AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets)
